html:
A mining town built in the desert of northern Niger, where a French-led company began producing uranium in 1971, followed by a second mine at Akouta in 1978.

Uranium from Arlit fed the nuclear power stations of France for decades and became Niger's main export, and the boom of the late 1970s paid for roads and schools under Seyni Kountche. When prices crashed in the 1980s the state fell into debt. Local Tuareg said they gained little and suffered from dust and radioactive waste, a grievance in the Tuareg rebellions. After the 2023 coup the military government pushed out the French operator.
